Israel and Iran have agreed to halt their strikes, according to multiple reports, with Netanyahu stating that "the fire on that front is contained." Tehran confirmed it had stopped military action hours earlier.

The ceasefire - if it holds - marks a significant de-escalation after weeks of direct exchanges between the two countries. The key question now is whether the pause is durable or simply a tactical pause while both sides reassess. Iran's missile arsenal, by recent U.S. intelligence estimates, remains largely intact, and the underlying disputes over Iran's nuclear program have not been resolved.

What a ceasefire buys is time. Whether anyone uses it productively is a different matter.

The Dispatch's Nick Catoggio argues that the United States is losing effective control over the trajectory of the Iran war - with Israel, not Washington, increasingly setting the pace and targets of the campaign.

The core tension: the Trump administration entered this conflict expecting to manage escalation, but Netanyahu's government has its own timeline and its own list of objectives that don't map cleanly onto American ones. Each Israeli strike that Washington didn't explicitly authorize narrows the space for U.S. diplomacy and makes a negotiated off-ramp harder to reach.

Catoggio's framing is worth sitting with. Wars tend to develop their own logic, and when two allies have different definitions of what "winning" looks like, the one willing to keep shooting usually ends up setting the terms. The open question is whether Washington has the leverage - or the will - to reassert it.

🤡🇵🇱🇺🇦 Poland is demanding participation in negotiations on the war in Ukraine - Reuters, citing a statement by Donald Tusk.

According to the Polish prime minister, Warsaw is dissatisfied with the "E3" negotiation format, which includes only the U.K., Germany, and France. This format excludes the participation of other European allies of Ukraine.

Tusk noted that he discussed this issue with Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni, who is also not enthusiastic about such an approach. He emphasised that any decisions or agreements made without Warsaw's participation will not be binding for Poland.

"I am very cautious about ideas being voiced in Western Europe regarding the early start of dialogue or negotiations with Putin on Ukraine," he stated.

Tusk also announced that a broader meeting dedicated to Ukraine will take place in the coming days. It is planned that representatives of Poland and Italy will join the leaders of the U.K., France, and Germany.
